rec: Empiric trial: standard-dose PPI 30–60 min before the first meal for 8 weeks in typical GERD.
PPIs are the most effective agents for healing erosive esophagitis and maintaining remission.
Eradicate H. pylori in all patients with active or past PUD; confirm eradication after therapy.
Bismuth quadruple therapy is a preferred 14-day regimen where clarithromycin resistance exceeds 15%.
PPI co-therapy for the duration of NSAID therapy in patients at elevated GI risk.
Combination topical retinoid + benzoyl peroxide is the preferred backbone for mild-to-moderate acne.
Topical antibiotics must be paired with benzoyl peroxide; never as monotherapy.
Isotretinoin is the most effective therapy for severe nodulocystic or scarring acne, with mandatory pregnancy prevention.
Topical metronidazole, azelaic acid, or ivermectin for papulopustular rosacea.
Subantimicrobial-dose doxycycline (40 mg) is effective and reduces resistance pressure.
Topical corticosteroids ± vitamin D analogs are first-line for mild plaque psoriasis.
Biologics (TNF/IL-17/IL-23 inhibitors) are highly effective for moderate-to-severe disease.
First-line classes: thiazides, ACE inhibitors, ARBs, CCBs — alone or in combination.
Beta-blockers are not first-line absent a compelling indication (CAD, HFrEF, arrhythmia).
Stage 2 HTN (≥140/90) or >20/10 mmHg above goal: initiate two first-line agents.
Metformin is the preferred initial agent for most patients.
SGLT2 inhibitor and/or GLP-1 RA with proven benefit for ASCVD, HF, or CKD — regardless of A1c.
Individualize A1c targets; <7% for most non-pregnant adults, relaxed with frailty/hypoglycemia risk.
As-needed low-dose ICS–formoterol is preferred for mild asthma; SABA-only is no longer recommended in adults/adolescents.
Controllers are ICS-based at every step; ICS–formoterol MART for moderate–severe disease.
Add LAMA or biologics (type-2 severe asthma) at higher steps.
Smoking cessation is the single most effective intervention; vaccination for influenza, pneumococcus, RSV, COVID-19.
Group E: LAMA + LABA, with ICS added guided by blood eosinophils.
SABA/SAMA as needed for all groups; LAMA preferred over LABA as monotherapy.
Outpatient, healthy, no resistance risk: amoxicillin or doxycycline.
Outpatient with comorbidity: amox-clav or cephalosporin + macrolide, or respiratory fluoroquinolone.
Empiric coverage must include atypical pathogens in most settings.
The WHO Essential Medicines List is the reference for national formularies; it includes core agents across analgesic, antimicrobial, cardiovascular, and endocrine classes.
High-intensity statin therapy for very-high-risk ASCVD prevention; LDL-C goals are lower than previous guidance (≥50% reduction, <55 mg/dL for very high risk).
Use narrow-spectrum agents first line; review antibiotics at 48–72 h; document indication, dose, and duration.
